subproblem.title: Two-sided eventual ball-mass bounds ⇒ Θ^n(μ, x) = a
subproblem.statement:
Let N, n ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on Euclidean N, x ∈ Euclidean N and a ∈ [0, ∞]; write ω_n = unitBallVolume n. Assume:
(i) for every c ∈ [0, ∞] with c < a · ω_n, eventually as t → 0⁺, c · ENNReal.ofReal(t)^n ≤ μ(closedBall x t);
(ii) for every c ∈ [0, ∞] with a · ω_n < c, eventually as t → 0⁺, μ(closedBall x t) ≤ c · ENNReal.ofReal(t)^n.
Then HasDensity n μ x a, i.e. μ(B_t(x))/(ω_n t^n) → a as t ↓ 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (x : Euclidean N) (a : ℝ≥0∞), (∀ c : ℝ≥0∞, c < a * unitBallVolume n → ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), c * ENNReal.ofReal t ^ n ≤ μ (closedBall x t)) → (∀ c : ℝ≥0∞, a * unitBallVolume n < c → ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), μ (closedBall x t) ≤ c * ENNReal.ofReal t ^ n) → HasDensity n μ x a
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 2, 7 and 8 of the parent proof. This is the final squeeze of Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2), carried out directly in [0, ∞].

Notation: ω := unitBallVolume n = volume(ball (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) 1); B_t(x) := closedBall x t. By definition, densityRatio n μ x t = μ(B_t(x)) / (ω · ENNReal.ofReal t ^ n), and HasDensity n μ x a means Tendsto (densityRatio n μ x) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 a).

Hypotheses:
(H₋) for every c < a · ω, ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] 0, c · ofReal(t)^n ≤ μ(B_t(x));
(H₊) for every c > a · ω, ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] 0, μ(B_t(x)) ≤ c · ofReal(t)^n.

1. 0 < ω < ∞. The open unit ball of EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) is nonempty and open, and volume there is an additive Haar measure, hence positive on nonempty open sets: ω > 0 (measure_ball_pos volume 0 one_pos). The ball is bounded in a proper space, so ω < ∞ (measure_ball_lt_top). (For n = 0 the space is a point, the ball is the whole space and ω = 1.)

2. The normalizer. For t > 0 put D_t := ω · ofReal(t)^n.
- D_t ≠ 0: ofReal(t) > 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_pos), so ofReal(t)^n ≠ 0, and ω ≠ 0.
- D_t ≠ ∞: ω ≠ ∞ and ofReal(t)^n ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.pow_ne_top, ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top).
By definition densityRatio n μ x t = μ(B_t(x)) / D_t.

3. Reduction. [0, ∞] carries the order topology, so by tendsto_order it suffices to show:
(a) for every b < a, ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] 0, b < densityRatio n μ x t;
(b) for every b > a, ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] 0, densityRatio n μ x t < b.

4. Proof of (a). Let b < a. Since [0, ∞] is densely ordered, pick b' with b < b' < a (exists_between). By step 1, right multiplication by ω is strictly monotone (ENNReal.mul_lt_mul_left with ω ≠ 0, ω ≠ ∞), so c := b' · ω < a · ω. By (H₋), ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] 0, c · ofReal(t)^n ≤ μ(B_t(x)). Also ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] 0, t > 0 (self_mem_nhdsWithin). For such t, by associativity, b' · D_t = (b' · ω) · ofReal(t)^n = c · ofReal(t)^n ≤ μ(B_t(x)). Hence b' ≤ μ(B_t(x)) / D_t by ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le, using D_t ≠ 0 and D_t ≠ ∞ from step 2. Therefore b < b' ≤ densityRatio n μ x t.

5. Proof of (b). Let b > a. Pick b' with a < b' < b (exists_between). As in step 4, c := b' · ω > a · ω. By (H₊), ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] 0, μ(B_t(x)) ≤ c · ofReal(t)^n = b' · (ω · ofReal(t)^n). ENNReal.div_le_of_le_mul (no side conditions) then gives μ(B_t(x)) / (ω · ofReal(t)^n) ≤ b', i.e. densityRatio n μ x t ≤ b' < b.

6. Conclusion. Steps 3–5 give Tendsto (densityRatio n μ x) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 a), which is HasDensity n μ x a. If a = ∞ then (b) is vacuous, and if a = 0 then (a) is vacuous, so the argument covers every a ∈ [0, ∞]. ∎
proof_key_steps: 0 < ω < ∞; for t > 0 the normalizer ω·ofReal(t)^n lies in (0,∞).
tendsto_order reduces the claim to: eventually b < ratio for every b < a, and eventually ratio < b for every b > a.
For b < a pick b < b' < a; apply the lower hypothesis with c = b'ω < aω and use ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le.
For b > a pick a < b' < b; apply the upper hypothesis with c = b'ω > aω and use ENNReal.div_le_of_le_mul.

audit.reason: The type exactly states the two eventual bounds for arbitrary a ∈ ℝ≥0∞. Positivity and finiteness of the normalizer justify lower-bound division; the cited upper-bound division lemma needs no additional conditions. Intermediate order bounds give the strict inequalities required by tendsto_order, including a = 0 and a = ∞. This independent lemma completes the selected parent assembly.

subproblem.title: Hausdorff measure of plane balls: H^n(T ∩ B_r(0)) = ω_n r^n
subproblem.statement: For N, n ∈ ℕ, T ∈ G(N,n) (Grassmannian N n) and r ∈ ℝ with r ≥ 0: μHE[n](T.plane ∩ closedBall 0 r) = unitBallVolume n · ENNReal.ofReal(r)^n, i.e. H^n(T ∩ B_r(0)) = ω_n r^n, where ω_n = unitBallVolume n = volume(ball (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) 1) and H^n = μHE[n] on Euclidean N.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (T : Grassmannian N n) (r : ℝ), 0 ≤ r → (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)) ((T.plane : Set (Euclidean N)) ∩ closedBall 0 r) = unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal r ^ n
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 3 of the parent proof. This is Simon's normalization of H^n, which agrees with Lebesgue measure on n-planes; it is the identity H^n(T ∩ B_ρ(0)) = ω_n ρ^n used in Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2). Notation: ℝ^n := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), ℝ^N := Euclidean N, H^n := μHE[n], ω := unitBallVolume n = volume(ball (0 : ℝ^n) 1).

1. Orthonormal coordinates on the plane. By Grassmannian.finrank_plane (SimonGMT Chapter08/Varifold.lean:126), finrank ℝ T.plane = n. Hence b := (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ T.plane).reindex (finCongr T.finrank_plane) is an orthonormal basis of T.plane indexed by Fin n, and e := b.repr.symm : ℝ^n ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] T.plane is a linear isometric equivalence.

2. The embedding. Let ι := T.plane.subtypeₗᵢ.comp e.toLinearIsometry : ℝ^n →ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℝ^N, so that ι v = ↑(e v) definitionally. ι is a linear isometry: ‖ι v‖ = ‖v‖ for all v (LinearIsometry.norm_map), and ι is an isometry of metric spaces (LinearIsometry.isometry).

3. Image of the ball: ι '' closedBall 0 r = T.plane ∩ closedBall 0 r.
(⊆) If ‖v‖ ≤ r, then ι v = ↑(e v) ∈ T.plane, and dist(ι v, 0) = ‖ι v‖ = ‖v‖ ≤ r.
(⊇) If y ∈ T.plane and ‖y‖ ≤ r, put v := e.symm ⟨y, hy⟩. Then ‖v‖ = ‖⟨y, hy⟩‖ = ‖y‖ ≤ r (LinearIsometryEquiv.norm_map; the norm of a submodule element is its ambient norm), and ι v = ↑(e (e.symm ⟨y, hy⟩)) = y (LinearIsometryEquiv.apply_symm_apply).

4. Isometry invariance. Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image (Mathlib Geometry/Euclidean/Volume/Measure.lean:131) applied to ι gives H^n(T.plane ∩ closedBall 0 r) = μHE[n](ι '' closedBall 0 r) = μHE[n](closedBall (0 : ℝ^n) r), where the last measure is the Euclidean Hausdorff measure on ℝ^n.

5. Hausdorff measure equals Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n. By EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume n (same file, line 187), μHE[n] = volume on ℝ^n, so the quantity equals volume(closedBall (0 : ℝ^n) r).

6. Scaling. Since r ≥ 0 and volume on ℝ^n is an additive Haar measure, Measure.addHaar_closedBall volume 0 hr gives volume(closedBall 0 r) = ENNReal.ofReal(r^(finrank ℝ ℝ^n)) · volume(ball 0 1). (This is Mathlib MeasureTheory/Measure/Lebesgue/EqHaar.lean:500, which has no Nontrivial hypothesis, so n = 0 is included.) Moreover finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin).

7. Conclusion. Since r ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal(r^n) = ENNReal.ofReal(r)^n (ENNReal.ofReal_pow), and volume(ball (0 : ℝ^n) 1) is by definition unitBallVolume n. Commuting the product gives μHE[n](T.plane ∩ closedBall 0 r) = unitBallVolume n · ENNReal.ofReal(r)^n. For n = 0 this reads H^0({0}) = 1 = ω_0. ∎
proof_key_steps: finrank T.plane = n, so e := ((stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ T.plane).reindex (finCongr T.finrank_plane)).repr.symm : ℝ^n ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] T.plane.
ι := T.plane.subtypeₗᵢ.comp e.toLinearIsometry is an isometry with ι '' closedBall 0 r = T.plane ∩ closedBall 0 r.
Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image and EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume reduce the left side to volume(closedBall (0 : ℝ^n) r).
Measure.addHaar_closedBall, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin and ENNReal.ofReal_pow give ENNReal.ofReal(r)^n · unitBallVolume n; commute the product.

audit.reason: Prose and Lean type agree, including r ≥ 0 and unrestricted natural dimensions. Orthonormal coordinates, the proved ball-image identity, isometry invariance and Haar scaling establish the formula. The scaling theorem requires no nontriviality assumption, so n = 0 and r = 0 are covered. The proof is complete and independent.

subproblem.title: Blow-up convergence ⇒ lower ball-mass bound c·t^n ≤ μ(B_t(x)) for c < θω_n
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on Euclidean N, x ∈ Euclidean N, T ∈ G(N,n) and θ ∈ ℝ with θ > 0. Assume that for every g ∈ C_c(Euclidean N, ℝ), t⁻¹^n ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) dμ(z) → θ ∫_{T.plane} g dμHE[n] as t → 0⁺. Then for every c ∈ [0, ∞] with c < ENNReal.ofReal(θ) · unitBallVolume n, eventually as t → 0⁺ we have c · ENNReal.ofReal(t)^n ≤ μ(closedBall x t).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (x : Euclidean N) (T : Grassmannian N n) (θ : ℝ), 0 < θ → (∀ g : C_c(Euclidean N, ℝ), Tendsto (fun t : ℝ ↦ t⁻¹ ^ n * ∫ z, g (t⁻¹ • (z - x)) ∂μ) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (θ * ∫ y in (T.plane : Set (Euclidean N)), g y ∂μHE[n]))) → ∀ c : ℝ≥0∞, c < ENNReal.ofReal θ * unitBallVolume n → ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), c * ENNReal.ofReal t ^ n ≤ μ (closedBall x t)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 2, 4 and 5 of the parent proof, which is the lower cutoff of Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2). The passage κ ↑ 1 of Step 7 is performed here by choosing κ in terms of c.

Notation: ω := unitBallVolume n; ν := μHE[n].restrict T.plane, so that ∫_T g dH^n = ∫ g dν; B_t(x) := closedBall x t; μ.real s := (μ s).toReal.

Hypotheses: θ > 0, and (Blow): for every g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ), t⁻¹^n ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) dμ(z) → θ ∫_T g dH^n as t → 0⁺. Fix c ∈ [0, ∞] with c < ofReal(θ) · ω.

1. ω ∈ (0, ∞). The open unit ball of EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) is nonempty and open, and volume is an additive Haar measure there, so ω > 0 (measure_ball_pos volume 0 one_pos) and ω < ∞ (measure_ball_lt_top). Hence ω.toReal > 0 (ENNReal.toReal_pos).

2. c is finite and c.toReal < θ · ω.toReal. Since c < ofReal θ · ω ≤ ∞, c ≠ ∞. Since θ ≥ 0 and ω ≠ ∞, ofReal θ · ω = ofReal(θ · ω.toReal) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, ENNReal.ofReal_toReal). Both c and ofReal(θ ω.toReal) are finite, so toReal preserves the strict inequality c < ofReal(θ ω.toReal) (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal). Finally toReal(ofReal(θ ω.toReal)) = θ ω.toReal because θ ω.toReal > 0.

3. Choice of κ. The map κ ↦ θ ω.toReal κ^n is continuous with value θ ω.toReal at κ = 1, so it tends to θ ω.toReal along 𝓝[<] 1 ((continuous_pow n).tendsto 1, then mono_left nhdsWithin_le_nhds, then const_mul). Since θ ω.toReal > c.toReal, eventually along 𝓝[<] 1 we have c.toReal < θ ω.toReal κ^n (lt_mem_nhds). Intersect with Ioo 0 1 ∈ 𝓝[<] 1 (Ioo_mem_nhdsLT zero_lt_one) and take a witness (Filter.Eventually.exists; 𝓝[<] 1 is NeBot). This gives κ with 0 < κ < 1 and c.toReal < θ ω.toReal κ^n.

4. Cutoff. For y ∈ ℝ^N let χ(y) := max(0, min(1, (1 − ‖y‖)/(1 − κ))).
- χ is continuous: it is built from the norm by continuous operations, and 1 − κ > 0.
- 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1.
- χ(y) = 1 whenever ‖y‖ ≤ κ, because then (1 − ‖y‖)/(1 − κ) ≥ 1.
- χ(y) = 0 whenever ‖y‖ ≥ 1, because then (1 − ‖y‖)/(1 − κ) ≤ 0.
So χ vanishes off the compact set closedBall 0 1 and has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro with isCompact_closedBall). Let g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ) be χ packaged with these proofs, so that g y = χ y.

5. Plane side: ω.toReal · κ^n ≤ ∫_T g dH^n. By Measure.restrict_apply (closed balls are measurable), ν(closedBall 0 s) = H^n(closedBall 0 s ∩ T.plane) = H^n(T.plane ∩ closedBall 0 s). The sibling lemma frt_td_plane_closedBall_hausdorff, with r = 1 and r = κ, then gives ν(closedBall 0 1) = ω · ofReal(1)^n < ∞ and ν(closedBall 0 κ) = ω · ofReal(κ)^n.
(i) g is ν-integrable. The indicator 1_{closedBall 0 1} is ν-integrable (integrable_indicator_iff and integrableOn_const, since the measure is finite). g is continuous, hence AE-strongly measurable. And |g(y)| ≤ 1_{closedBall 0 1}(y) for all y, since g ≤ 1 and g(y) = 0 when ‖y‖ > 1. So Integrable.mono' applies.
(ii) Pointwise 0 ≤ 1_{closedBall 0 κ} ≤ g, since g = 1 on closedBall 0 κ and g ≥ 0 elsewhere.
By integral_mono_of_nonneg, ∫ 1_{closedBall 0 κ} dν ≤ ∫ g dν. Moreover ∫ 1_{closedBall 0 κ} dν = ν.real(closedBall 0 κ) (integral_indicator_one) = (ω · ofReal(κ)^n).toReal = ω.toReal · κ^n (ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_pow, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal with κ ≥ 0).

6. The limit exceeds c. By step 5 and θ ≥ 0, then step 3, θ ∫_T g dH^n ≥ θ · ω.toReal κ^n > c.toReal. Apply (Blow) to g; since the limit lies in the open set (c.toReal, ∞) (lt_mem_nhds), we get ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] 0, c.toReal < t⁻¹^n ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) dμ(z). Also ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] 0, t > 0 (self_mem_nhdsWithin). Fix t with both properties; it remains to show c · ofReal(t)^n ≤ μ(B_t(x)).

7. Comparison with the ball mass. If μ(B_t(x)) = ∞ the inequality is trivial (le_top). Otherwise 1_{B_t(x)} is μ-integrable, and for every z we have 0 ≤ g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) ≤ 1_{B_t(x)}(z):
- if z ∈ B_t(x), use g ≤ 1;
- if z ∉ B_t(x), then ‖z − x‖ > t, so ‖t⁻¹ • (z − x)‖ = ‖z − x‖/t > 1 (norm_smul, t > 0) and g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) = 0.
integral_mono_of_nonneg (which needs integrability only of the larger function) together with integral_indicator_one gives ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) dμ ≤ μ.real(B_t(x)).

8. Conclusion. Multiply the inequality of step 6 by t^n > 0. Since t⁻¹^n · t^n = 1, c.toReal · t^n < (t⁻¹^n ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) dμ) · t^n = ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) dμ ≤ μ.real(B_t(x)). Since c ≠ ∞, c.toReal ≥ 0 and t ≥ 0, c · ofReal(t)^n = ofReal(c.toReal) · ofReal(t^n) = ofReal(c.toReal · t^n) (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal, ENNReal.ofReal_pow, ENNReal.ofReal_mul). This is ≤ ofReal(μ.real(B_t(x))) (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal), which equals μ(B_t(x)) because μ(B_t(x)) ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal). ∎
proof_key_steps: ω ∈ (0,∞); c is finite and c.toReal < θ·ω.toReal.
Choose κ ∈ (0,1) with c.toReal < θ·ω.toReal·κ^n by continuity of κ^n at κ = 1.
Cutoff g(y) = max(0, min(1, (1−‖y‖)/(1−κ))) ∈ C_c: equals 1 on closedBall 0 κ, vanishes for ‖y‖ ≥ 1, 0 ≤ g ≤ 1.
Sibling plane lemma: g is H^n⌞T-integrable and ∫_T g ≥ H^n(T ∩ B_κ(0)).toReal = ω.toReal·κ^n, so θ∫_T g > c.toReal.
Blow-up limit: eventually t⁻¹^n ∫ g(t⁻¹(z−x)) dμ > c.toReal with t > 0.
g(t⁻¹(z−x)) ≤ 1_{B_t(x)}(z) gives ∫ ≤ μ.real(B_t(x)) when μ(B_t(x)) is finite (trivial otherwise); convert to c·ofReal(t)^n ≤ μ(B_t(x)).

subproblem.title: Blow-up convergence + local finiteness ⇒ upper ball-mass bound μ(B_t(x)) ≤ c·t^n for c > θω_n
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on Euclidean N, x ∈ Euclidean N, T ∈ G(N,n) and θ, r₀ ∈ ℝ with θ > 0, r₀ > 0 and μ(closedBall x r₀) ≠ ∞. Assume that for every g ∈ C_c(Euclidean N, ℝ), t⁻¹^n ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) dμ(z) → θ ∫_{T.plane} g dμHE[n] as t → 0⁺. Then for every c ∈ [0, ∞] with ENNReal.ofReal(θ) · unitBallVolume n < c, eventually as t → 0⁺ we have μ(closedBall x t) ≤ c · ENNReal.ofReal(t)^n.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (x : Euclidean N) (T : Grassmannian N n) (θ r₀ : ℝ), 0 < θ → 0 < r₀ → μ (closedBall x r₀) ≠ ⊤ → (∀ g : C_c(Euclidean N, ℝ), Tendsto (fun t : ℝ ↦ t⁻¹ ^ n * ∫ z, g (t⁻¹ • (z - x)) ∂μ) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (θ * ∫ y in (T.plane : Set (Euclidean N)), g y ∂μHE[n]))) → ∀ c : ℝ≥0∞, ENNReal.ofReal θ * unitBallVolume n < c → ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), μ (closedBall x t) ≤ c * ENNReal.ofReal t ^ n
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 2, 4 and 6 of the parent proof. This is the upper cutoff (f ≡ 1 on B_1(0), f ≡ 0 off B_{1+ε}(0)) of Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2). The passage κ ↓ 1 of Step 7 is performed here by choosing κ in terms of c.

Notation: ω := unitBallVolume n; ν := μHE[n].restrict T.plane; B_t(x) := closedBall x t; μ.real s := (μ s).toReal.

Hypotheses: θ > 0, r₀ > 0, μ(B_{r₀}(x)) ≠ ∞, and (Blow): for every g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ), t⁻¹^n ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) dμ(z) → θ ∫_T g dH^n as t → 0⁺. Fix c ∈ [0, ∞] with ofReal(θ) · ω < c.

1. ω ∈ (0, ∞) and ω.toReal > 0, by measure_ball_pos and measure_ball_lt_top on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) and ENNReal.toReal_pos.

2. The case c = ∞. For every t > 0, ofReal(t)^n ≠ 0, so ∞ · ofReal(t)^n = ∞ (ENNReal.top_mul) and μ(B_t(x)) ≤ ∞. Since {t | t > 0} ∈ 𝓝[>] 0 (self_mem_nhdsWithin), the claim holds. Assume from now on that c ≠ ∞.

3. θ · ω.toReal < c.toReal. We have ofReal θ · ω = ofReal(θ ω.toReal) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, ENNReal.ofReal_toReal), so ofReal(θ ω.toReal) < c with both sides finite. Applying toReal (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal, then ENNReal.toReal_ofReal with θ ω.toReal > 0) gives the claim.

4. Choice of κ. The map κ ↦ θ ω.toReal κ^n is continuous and equals θ ω.toReal < c.toReal at κ = 1. So along 𝓝[>] 1 it eventually satisfies θ ω.toReal κ^n < c.toReal (gt_mem_nhds), and eventually κ > 1 (self_mem_nhdsWithin). Pick such a κ: κ > 1 (hence κ > 0) and θ ω.toReal κ^n < c.toReal.

5. Cutoff. For y ∈ ℝ^N let χ(y) := max(0, min(1, (κ − ‖y‖)/(κ − 1))).
- χ is continuous and 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1.
- χ(y) = 1 if ‖y‖ ≤ 1, because then (κ − ‖y‖)/(κ − 1) ≥ 1.
- χ(y) = 0 if ‖y‖ ≥ κ, because then the quotient is ≤ 0.
So χ vanishes off the compact set closedBall 0 κ and has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro). Let g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ) be χ, so that g y = χ y.

6. Plane side: ∫_T g dH^n ≤ ω.toReal · κ^n. By the sibling lemma frt_td_plane_closedBall_hausdorff with r = κ, and Measure.restrict_apply, ν(closedBall 0 κ) = H^n(T.plane ∩ closedBall 0 κ) = ω · ofReal(κ)^n < ∞. Hence 1_{closedBall 0 κ} is ν-integrable (integrable_indicator_iff, integrableOn_const). Moreover 0 ≤ g ≤ 1_{closedBall 0 κ} pointwise, since g ≤ 1 everywhere and g(y) = 0 when ‖y‖ > κ. By integral_mono_of_nonneg and integral_indicator_one, ∫ g dν ≤ ν.real(closedBall 0 κ) = (ω · ofReal(κ)^n).toReal = ω.toReal · κ^n.

7. The limit is below c. By θ ≥ 0, step 6 and step 4, θ ∫_T g dH^n ≤ θ ω.toReal κ^n < c.toReal. Applying (Blow) to g (gt_mem_nhds), ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] 0, t⁻¹^n ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) dμ(z) < c.toReal. Also ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] 0, t ∈ (0, r₀/κ) (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT, since r₀/κ > 0). Fix t with both properties.

8. Finiteness. From t < r₀/κ we get κt ≤ r₀; from κ ≥ 1 and t > 0 we get t ≤ κt. Hence B_t(x) ⊆ B_{κt}(x) ⊆ B_{r₀}(x) (closedBall_subset_closedBall), and μ(B_t(x)) ≤ μ(B_{κt}(x)) ≤ μ(B_{r₀}(x)) < ∞ (measure_mono).

9. Integrability of the rescaled cutoff. For every z, ‖t⁻¹ • (z − x)‖ = ‖z − x‖/t (norm_smul, t > 0). The function z ↦ g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) is continuous, hence AE-strongly measurable. It satisfies |g(t⁻¹ • (z − x))| ≤ 1_{B_{κt}(x)}(z): if z ∉ B_{κt}(x) then ‖z − x‖ > κt, so ‖t⁻¹ • (z − x)‖ > κ and g(·) = 0; otherwise |g| ≤ 1. Since μ(B_{κt}(x)) < ∞ the indicator is μ-integrable, so Integrable.mono' shows that z ↦ g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) is μ-integrable.

10. Comparison. For every z, 0 ≤ 1_{B_t(x)}(z) ≤ g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)): if z ∈ B_t(x) then ‖t⁻¹ • (z − x)‖ = ‖z − x‖/t ≤ 1 and g(·) = 1; otherwise the indicator is 0 ≤ g(·). By integral_mono_of_nonneg (using step 9) and integral_indicator_one, μ.real(B_t(x)) ≤ ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) dμ.

11. Conclusion. With t^n > 0, μ.real(B_t(x)) ≤ ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) dμ = (t⁻¹^n ∫ g(t⁻¹ • (z − x)) dμ) · t^n < c.toReal · t^n by step 7. Since μ(B_t(x)) ≠ ∞, μ(B_t(x)) = ofReal(μ.real(B_t(x))) ≤ ofReal(c.toReal · t^n) = ofReal(c.toReal) · ofReal(t)^n = c · ofReal(t)^n (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal, ENNReal.ofReal_mul, ENNReal.ofReal_pow, and ENNReal.ofReal_toReal with c ≠ ∞). ∎
